title: Responsibility: technology decisions and why to document them

videos.script: Every architecture is a pile of decisions, and most of them were never written down. {{title}} This lesson is about technology decisions, and about leaving a trail behind them. At Carreto, the Tracking team has to choose where a hundred GPS positions a second will live. {{tracking}} Renata does not pick the winner. She asks six questions, among them whether the team can run it and what it would cost to leave. {{questions}} Then there is the question of how much care a choice deserves. Some decisions are two-way doors, and you can walk back through them in an afternoon. Others are one-way doors that reach other teams, and those get the architect's attention. {{doors}} One of them is how Payments learns that a delivery was proved, and you will read its record whole. Context, decision, consequences, and the options it turned down. {{record}} An accepted record is never edited. When the decision changes, a new record replaces it, and the old reasoning stays readable. {{supersede}} Last, why bother at all. There is the engineer about to delete a job that looks useless, and the meeting that keeps coming back. And there is the person who decided, who deserves to be judged by what was known at the time. {{why}}
